title: Add an in-tool agent onboarding/capabilities contract
recommendation: Add `rpce-headless capabilities --json` and `rpce-headless robot-docs guide` or an equivalent MCP `headless_capabilities` tool. Include loaded-root semantics, stdio vs restricted/full socket tool exposure, recommended onboarding sequence, context_builder lifecycle, agent_manage/list_agents then agent_run pattern, oracle opt-in guidance, fake-agent fixture caveat, exit codes, and smoke commands.

title: Make help first-try friendly and exit 0
recommendation: Teach top-level and subcommands to accept `--help`/`-h` and exit 0. Bare `rpce-headless` should either exit 0 with concise help or offer the exact command to run. Include `serve --help`, `dump --help`, `connect --help`, and `context-build --help` tests.

title: Document and encode the read-only subagent pattern
recommendation: Make the server-managed subagent flow explicit in docs and in-tool robot docs as an optional independent-review path after status triage and Context Builder: call `agent_manage list_agents`, choose an available real/low-cost agent, start bounded read-only `agent_run` tasks, poll/wait, get logs, cleanup sessions, and integrate with direct file evidence. The flow should bless context_builder as the default architecture-onboarding path and read-only agent_run as an optional second pass, while keeping oracle opt-in.
evidence: session line 233: direct archaeology succeeded but did not use context_builder/agent_run

title: Teach fallback when code structure is unavailable
recommendation: When `get_code_structure` has no codemap for a path/language, return a useful hint that names `file_search` and `read_file` fallback commands. Consider adding common TS/Python codemap support later, but the immediate ergonomic fix is an error/result that teaches the next move.
evidence: session evidence: get_code_structure returned no structure for TS/Python files

title: Expose loaded root explicitly in a lightweight status/capabilities response
recommendation: Root negotiation now works, but agents still infer the loaded root from tree text. Add `loaded_roots` to capabilities/status/robot-docs, or make `workspace_context include:["tree","tokens"]` visibly include root metadata in structuredContent.
evidence: session line 27: root had to be inferred from tree label

title: Simplify context_builder schema discovery
recommendation: Either split one-shot and async lifecycle into clearer tool surfaces, or enrich the existing schema descriptions with concrete examples for synchronous clarify, async start/wait/get_result, timeout vs timeout_seconds, cleanup, and unsupported export_response. The README explains this, but schema-only agents face a lot of branching in one tool.

title: Add compact status JSON for first-call workspace triage
recommendation: Add `rpce-headless robot-docs status --json` and MCP `headless_status` so agents can verify root metadata, root mismatch warnings, MCP exposure, available agent tools, suggested first calls, architecture onboarding, and smoke commands in one compact packet. Keep `robot-docs triage --json` as a forgiving alias.
evidence: Pass 3 functional discovery: capabilities/dump/workspace_context were split across multiple calls

title: Return structured no-codemap evidence from get_code_structure
recommendation: When a requested path resolves but has no codemap, return structured content naming the file, status `codemap_unavailable`, unresolved paths, and fallback tools `file_search` and `read_file`, while preserving readable text content for MCP clients.
evidence: Pass 2 handoff queued structured get_code_structure fallback payloads

title: Make architecture onboarding a first-class status/capabilities block
recommendation: Expose a paste-ready architecture onboarding recipe in status JSON, capabilities JSON, robot docs, README, and AGENTS.md: confirm roots with headless_status, start context_builder for curated architecture synthesis, then use get_file_tree, file_search, get_code_structure, and read_file for verification anchors and citations.
evidence: Pass 3 functional focus: architecture workflow should be obvious from the first status call

title: Promote Context Builder and server-managed subagents in tool discovery
recommendation: Black-box trials showed agents can see context_builder and agent_run yet still default to repeated get_file_tree/file_search/read_file calls. Order tools/list as headless_status, headless_capabilities, context_builder, agent_manage, agent_run before direct file reads; describe context_builder as the preferred repo-onboarding/planning tool; describe agent_manage/agent_run as the rpce-headless server-managed optional independent-review lifecycle and explicitly distinguish it from client-local ad hoc subagents.
evidence: Black-box skill-climb session 019ed290-2ddc-7623-ae86-ac9ce14b9514 used 21 read_file calls, 11 file_search calls, and no context_builder or agent_run despite tool discovery exposing them

title: Expose native RepoPrompt workflow shapes in headless status/capabilities
recommendation: Expose the native RepoPrompt product workflow grammar separately from Smithers: role labels explore/engineer/pair/design, scoped subagent rules, custom workflow extension points, and the investigate/optimize/deep_plan choreography. Teach agents to gather cheap/narrow evidence, use context_builder for curated selection and synthesis, then hand stronger pair/design agents shared evidence instead of making every reviewer run a full research tree. Mark custom workflows honestly as metadata-only in headless v1 until workflow listing/resolution/settings mutation is implemented.
evidence: Product workflow prompts encode delegation shapes in WorkflowPrompt+Investigate.swift, WorkflowPrompt+Optimize.swift, WorkflowPrompt+DeepPlan.swift, role labels in MCPAgentControlToolProvider.swift, and custom markdown workflow storage in AgentWorkflowStore.swift

title: Make Context Builder recoverable after MCP client timeouts
recommendation: Black-box testing showed the improved first-call guidance successfully pushed agents to context_builder, but synchronous context_builder could exceed the MCP client's two-minute tools/call ceiling. After timeout, a follow-up op=start returned 'already running' without a pollable context_id, and context_id 'active' reported expired. Route compatibility one-shot calls through the async run registry, cap the synchronous wait below the MCP client timeout, return a running snapshot with context_id when still active, and let context_id active/current resolve to the current run.
evidence: Codex session 019ed2d2-e725-7280-9e48-4fd26cc6282d: context_builder timed out after 119.999s, op=start returned already running, poll active returned expired

title: Expose Context Builder progress in headless MCP waits
recommendation: Black-box retesting showed agents now start context_builder correctly, but then pass timeout_seconds to op=wait and sit through silent two-minute MCP calls. Accept timeout_seconds as an op=wait alias, cap wait windows to progress-friendly snapshots, emit MCP notifications/progress when clients provide a progress token, and include started_at, elapsed_seconds, and next_action in run snapshots.
evidence: Codex session 019ed2df-a02a-72d2-9bc5-4914647f39c4: op=start succeeded, op=wait used timeout_seconds, parser ignored it and defaulted to a silent 120s wait

title: Make headless_status honest on discovery-restricted sockets
recommendation: Make headless_status reflect the transport serving the request. On discovery-restricted sockets, report only direct evidence tools as available here, do not suggest context_builder/agent_manage/agent_run/oracle_send as first calls, and point agents to full stdio or authenticated full-tool sockets for advanced workflows.
evidence: Side review found restricted sockets expose headless_status but block the full-only tools it advertised as available and suggested as next calls
